before_taxonomy.classification_basis: The company attributes false director payment instructions to deepfake/profile-cloning impersonation and reports employee transfers. primary_classification.classification_basis: The company’s primary disclosure attributes false director payment instructions to deepfake/profile-cloning methods and reports that the employee acted on them, transferring ₹10.70 crore. This supports materially AI-mediated false authority inducing an economic decision while keeping the precise synthetic technique attributed and unresolved.

secondary_classifications.classification_basis: The issuer reports deepfake/profile-cloning impersonation of its identifiable director by unknown actors who had no authority to issue the director’s instructions. Profile cloning is an identity-bound reproduction of the director’s representation for another purpose; the requester-side use of the person-bound profile as sufficient authority for that portrayal supports the class. The precise source media and generator remain unknown, limiting confidence.
Reported deepfake director impersonation made transfer instructions appear authorised; the employee sent subsidiary funds before the real director denied the instruction.

after_taxonomy.classification_basis: The company attributes false director payment instructions to deepfake/profile-cloning impersonation and reports employee transfers. The economic deception, unauthorised identity representation and resulting trust-based transfer are independently identified. Technical synthesis and device compromise remain company-attributed. The reported cloned director profile materially executed the false instruction; the employee transferred funds believing it genuine, and the director denied issuing it. This independently establishes impaired choice under the human-directed scope of the current manipulation criteria, without asserting an autonomous AI objective.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The filing identifies review of controls after the event but does not establish an available and applicable preincident protective control with a defined activation trigger.
